title: Bunny Blue and the Sparkly Star
markdown:
Bunny Blue lived in a cozy burrow at the edge of a garden that always smelled like sunshine and sweet ripe strawberries. His fur was the softest blue, like a new egg, and his long ears would droop just a little bit when he was thinking very hard. His very best friend in the whole wide world was Squeak the gerbil, a tiny fizz of whiskers and lots and lots of energy who loved to explore every single nook and cranny of their sunny world.

One bright cheerful morning, as Bunny Blue and Squeak were busy rolling a plump rosy apple across the dewy green grass, their eyes caught sight of something very, very nice. Just beyond the tall daisies, where the garden path curved like a smile, was a puddle! Not a big muddy puddle. A bright sparkly puddle, showing the blue sky like a mirror. And floating right in the very middle, bobbing gently as if on a tiny swing, was a beautiful paper star. It was the colour of the sky just before bedtime, a soft dusky blue, sprinkled with tiny silver sparkles that winked in the sunlight.

“Wow!” squeaked Squeak, his tail wiggling. “Bunny Blue, look at that sparkly star! It looks so lonely out there all by itself!”

Bunny Blue twitched his nose, soft blue fur rippling. “It does,” he said softly. “But… but it’s on the water.” A tiny shiver went through his fluffy blue fur. Water was wet. And sometimes puddles could feel very big indeed, like little lakes. He liked his paws to be perfectly dry and his fur to be wonderfully fluffy. He didn’t want the star to get all soggy and sad, but he also didn’t fancy a wet paw himself. It felt like a tiny pebble in his shoe.

“We must save it!” declared Squeak, already hopping up and down. “We must go on a big adventure!”

Bunny Blue looked at Squeak’s happy bright face, then back at the lonely pretty star. If they didn’t do something very soon, the star might just drift away, carried by the tiniest breeze. And that would be such a shame. He knew Squeak was right. They must help the star. But how?

Suddenly his long blue ears perked straight up. “I know! Mrs. Higgins left her little toy boat by the bird bath yesterday! It’s just our size, I bet!”

And so Bunny Blue and Squeak hurried together, feet padding softly on the grass, over to where the little red toy boat sat waiting by the tall bird bath. Bright red wood. Very sturdy. Perfect for little adventurers.

“This will be perfect!” chirped Squeak, already clambering nimbly aboard. Bunny Blue took a big breath and carefully stepped in, blue fur puffing out a little. The boat wiggled ever so slightly, and Bunny Blue’s heart went thump-thump.

They pushed off from the grassy edge. The puddle, which had looked so wide from the garden path, now felt like a big ocean stretching out before them.

“Steady now, Bunny Blue!” called Squeak, using a small smooth twig like a tiny paddle. “We’re on our way to rescue the star!”

Bunny Blue held the sides of the boat tight, gaze fixed with all his might on the beautiful paper star. He tried very hard not to look at the shimmering water all around, which sparkled so much it almost made his eyes blink. A big wobbly green leaf floated past, making the boat wobble just a tiny bit. Bunny Blue squeezed his eyes shut for a second. His whiskers wiggled. He could hear the gentle lapping of the water, feel the smooth cool wood beneath his paws, see the bright dazzling sunlight dancing on the ripples. Then he heard Squeak’s cheerful happy humming and bravely opened his eyes again. A friendly ladybug with seven perfect black spots crawled onto the very edge of the boat, giving them a cheerful little wave with one antenna before buzzing away. Bunny Blue felt a little bit braver.

Slowly, ever so slowly and carefully, they glided closer and closer. Squeak reached out with his twig paddle and gently nudged the star toward them. “Almost there, almost there!” With a final careful push, the star slid right into their little red boat! Hooray!

But as they turned the boat around to go back to the soft grass, they noticed a new problem. The boat, nudged by the star’s gentle weight, had drifted further away from the grass than they had realized. The edge seemed like a very long hop indeed.

Bunny Blue’s ears drooped. They had the star, oh yes, but how would they get it back safely without getting wet? The water looked so deep now, like a big blue blanket.

“Oh dear, oh dear,” he murmured, voice small.

Squeak looked worried too. Then he had a good idea. “We can push it to the lily pad!” He pointed with his twig. Near the edge of the puddle, like a little green island, was a big green lily pad. “If we push the star onto the lily pad, it will be safe there, and then we can get our boat back to the bank!”

This was the hardest part. Bunny Blue knew they had to be very, very careful now. The star was so important. He imagined the wetness, the splash, the star slipping. A tremor in his soft paws. What if it falls off? What if it sinks right to the bottom? He took another deep breath. He wanted to help the star more than he wanted to stay perfectly dry. He thought of Squeak, so brave and so small, who needed his help.

Slowly, carefully, he nudged the paper star with his soft blue nose. It slid toward the edge of the boat, then gently, ever so gently, onto the smooth cool green surface of the lily pad. He could smell the damp earth from the lily pad, feel the cool slickness of its waxy surface, and hear the faint gentle gurgle of water as the star settled perfectly in the middle.

With the star safely resting on its own little green island, Bunny Blue and Squeak turned their little red boat around and paddled with all their might toward the soft grass. They bumped gently against the welcoming soil, and Bunny Blue hopped out, his paws as dry and fluffy as ever! Squeak scampered after him, doing a little jig of joy. They stood together and watched the paper star sit proudly on its lily pad, safe and sound, shining like a little beacon.

Bunny Blue looked at the puddle, then at the lily pad. He hadn’t gotten wet at all! Not one little splash! And he had helped rescue the sparkly star. A warm happy feeling spread through him, much better than the tiny pebble of worry. He stood up a little taller, blue fur looking even brighter in the sunshine.

“We did it, Squeak!”

Squeak did a happy little dance, tail a blur. The sparkly star, safe on its lily pad, seemed to wink at them. Bunny Blue’s ears, which had drooped so often that morning, stayed up. The apple waited in the grass, still plump and rosy, and the puddle kept showing the sky, as if it had always been a friendly mirror and not a lake at all.
characters: Bunny Blue (a garden bunny), Squeak (the gerbil)
author: StoryGen Community
